answer: A stake-weighted reputation signal makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a refundable deposit that is slashed when peers flag its attestations as false, so spawning thousands of sock-puppets costs real capital instead of free usernames. Like saffron harvested flower by flower from a vast ocean of cheap claims, only identities backed by verifiable work and locked stake rise to the top, while Sybil farms drown in their own deposit costs.
